items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: In 1948 I got a call from Bobby Tucker to join him to work with Billie Holiday... So we got together... And I stayed with Billie I guess maybe about, about a year. And we traveled.

ctx.x: Was he doing Louis Armstrong at that time?

Louis Armstrong, Dizzy, you name it. Especially trumpet players. He had Red Allen and Higginbotham and that group, the Dixieland groups. He had control over all of these different groups — Billie Holiday and you name it — Dinah Washington, he had all of these people. And so I got to know him first by just sending, make sure I sent that commission into him. So he sort of got a respect for me as a business person. So in 1944 © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

we got a job to go to 52nd Street and open in the Onyx Club. And in those days they gave you a long term deal, so the deal was for six months. And Jimmy Jones, I’m sort of ahead of myself, because actually Jimmy Jones joined the group — Raymond Walters was the first pianist with us, and he worked with us maybe in Chicago for maybe about two or three months. And then Jimmy Jones and I had been friends, I knew him as a player and I recommended that he come on with us. And that’s how the real Stuff Smith Trio got…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Bobby called me to ask me if I would join the group to accompany Billie at this particular concert... We spent time – Denzil and I would go out to his house. We would rehearse with Billie.

ctx.x: Can you tell us about that, how she got in touch with you? Or how you . . .?

She didn’t get in touch with me at all. I knew Billie, because I’d seen her work before on 52nd Street. But it was through Bobby Tucker, who was her accompanist and who did the arrangements for her and worked for her. When she came out of Lexington, which was the rehab place while she was away for dope – when that was over, that period was over, and she was allowed to – out to work again, she came – stayed at Bobby’s home. She was very close. He was like family with her, Bobby Tucker. Bobby wanted to start…

which turned out it didn’t work out that way, because Joe was a gangster, and when the gangsters got through talking to this man, he was no longer a part of the picture.
